pl-l3d39c3-d1e112.summary: Holds it better to believe that one perjures who swears what is false with will to deceive, who swears what is false thinking it true, and who swears what is true thinking it false.
claims: There are three ways of perjuring.

pl-l3d39c3-d1e115.summary: Quotes Augustine: men swear falsely when they deceive or are deceived: either one thinks true what is false and swears rashly, or knows or thinks it false and swears it as true, wickedly. One who thinks true what is false is deceived, not perjuring from the heart; one who knows it false and swears it true is a detestable beast; one who thinks it false and swears it true, even if it is true (as that it rained), is a perjurer. It matters how the word proceeds from the mind: only a guilty mind makes a guilty tongue.
claims: Swearing what one knows is false is detestable.
Swearing what one thinks false is perjury even if it is true.
Only a guilty mind makes a guilty tongue.

pl-l3d39c3-d1e124.summary: Draws out that these words teach that man perjures in three ways: knowingly swearing falsehood, swearing what is true thinking it false, or swearing what is false thinking it true.

pl-l3d39c3-d1e127.summary: Objects that the last case does not seem to be perjury, or, if called perjury because something false is sworn, the swearer does not seem guilty, since his mind is not guilty and so neither is his tongue.

pl-l3d39c3-d1e131.summary: Replies that his mind is guilty in presuming to swear what he has not clearly ascertained to be true. So not all perjury is a lie, nor does everyone who perjures lie; but everyone who swears lying perjures, and everyone who swears what is false, lying or not, perjures.
claims: Swearing without certainty makes the mind guilty.
Not all perjury is a lie, but all false swearing is perjury.

pl-l3d39c3-d1e134.summary: Asks what the perjury is when someone swears what is true, thinking it false: the meaning of the words is true, so it is neither false nor a lie, and what is true does not seem to be perjury.

pl-l3d39c3-d1e137.summary: Answers that speaking against one's mind under the attestation of an oath is perjury; lying with an oath is perjury. So perjury is swearing what is false with intent to deceive, swearing what is false without intent to deceive, or swearing what is true with intent to deceive.
claims: Speaking against one's mind under oath is perjury.

pl-l3d39c3-d1e140.summary: Objects: if everyone who swears falsely perjures, then one who swears to give something by a set date and does not do it perjured from the moment he swore, since it was not going to happen as he swore.

pl-l3d39c3-d1e143.summary: Replies that not everyone who swears what turns out false perjures from the moment he swears, as in this case; such an oath becomes perjury with guilt from the moment he changes his purpose or passes the deadline.
claims: A sworn promise becomes perjury when one changes purpose or passes the deadline.

pl-l3d39c3.summary: Holds it better to say that one perjures who swears falsely to deceive, who swears falsely thinking it true, and who swears truly thinking it false. Augustine distinguishes those who swear falsely when they deceive or are deceived, and notes that one who swears it rained, thinking it did not, perjures even if it did rain: only a guilty mind makes a guilty tongue. Against the objection that one deceived is not guilty, Lombard answers that his mind is guilty in presuming to swear what he has not clearly ascertained. So not all perjury is lying, but all who swear lying perjure and all who swear falsely perjure. Speaking against one's mind under oath is perjury, even when the words are true. One who swears to give something by a fixed date does not perjure at once, but becomes guilty when he changes purpose or misses the deadline.
claims: One perjures who swears falsely to deceive, swears falsely thinking it true, or swears truly thinking it false.
One who swears rashly to something false has a guilty mind for presuming to swear.
Not all perjury is lying, but all false swearing is perjury.
Swearing against one's mind is perjury even if the statement is true.
A sworn promise becomes perjury when one changes purpose or misses the term.
